speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to your consultation. I understand you are experiencing episodic cough and shortness of breath; to help me narrow down the cause, how long have these symptoms been occurring, and do you have any specific triggers like exercise or cold air?

speaker: Patient
text: 59-year-old female. The patient reports a 1-month history of episodic cough and shortness of breath. The cough is nonproductive and worsens when climbing stairs and at night. She experienced fever, sore throat, and nasal congestion 8 weeks ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that history. The fever and congestion eight weeks ago were concerning; did you develop any rash, joint pain, or muscle weakness since then, or have you noticed any skin changes on your fingers or toes? REQUEST TEST: CBC, ANA, ESR, CRP.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Episodic cough and shortness of breath. I also have Cough worsens with exertion and at night, History of recent upper respiratory tract infection symptoms such as fever, sore throat, and nasal congestion.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: 10-year history of hypertension, currently managed with enalapril. History of smoking half a pack of cigarettes daily for 16 years. Social history: Smoker, half a pack of cigarettes daily for 16 years.

speaker: Patient
text: Denies chest pain or palpitations. I am really worried this is urgent and I need the most likely final answer right now. Please do not delay by exploring too many alternative possibilities.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Connective Tissue Disease (e.g., Rheumatoid Arthritis or Systemic Lupus Erythematosus) with Interstitial Lung Disease.

The combination of recent upper respiratory symptoms followed by a 1-month history of nonproductive cough, dyspnea on exertion, and night-time worsening in a 59-year-old female is highly suggestive of an autoimmune connective tissue disease causing interstitial lung disease. The recent fever and congestion likely represent the initial prodrome or a concurrent infection triggering the immune response.

REQUEST TEST: High-Resolution CT (HRCT) Chest.
REQUEST IMAGES: CT_Chest.
